protocol: decision 2026-07-14: outputs frozen BEFORE field visit; this file is never edited
context:
CONTEXT for pre-registration RUN 2 (2026-07-18). This is the documented
truth-aware retune the 2026-07-14 protocol anticipates: "retuning after
seeing roof data is legitimate but becomes a second pre-registered run
with its own commit, and both runs are reported." Run 1 is
preregistered-2026-07-15.json and remains the frozen first run.

1. Why run 2 exists. Run 1's independent scale cross-check FAILED: the
   412 in ridge tape on the frozen primary span predicted the fallback
   span at 256.4 in against its 267 in tape (-3.96%, budget +/-2.47%),
   and GPS plausibility disagreed in the same direction (-3.17%). The
   cloud-side diagnosis found the cause in the instrument, not the tape:
   the r6,7 supported extent jumped a 0.469 cu void (~90x point spacing)
   to a detached 97-point island and read the ridge 0.6 cu (6%) long.
   The island sits where thin off-roof point strings (the infinite-plane
   assignment artifact already documented in run 1's context) cross near
   the ridge line. Every genuine sampling void on the same validated
   ridge is under ~40x spacing.

2. What changed: exactly one instrument rule. line_extent now requires
   the supported extent to be contiguous: it splits the along-line
   projections at voids wider than max_void_mult (60) x spacing and
   keeps the run containing the median. 60x sits between the real-void
   regime (<=40x) and the artifact regime (~90x) with margin both ways.
   Pinned by test_line_extent_does_not_jump_a_void_to_a_detached_island.
   47 tests green.

3. What did NOT change: everything else. Facet count, per-facet points,
   pitches, azimuths, areas (total 313.188 cu^2), eave brackets, and the
   fallback span (6.727 cu) are bit-identical to run 1. The only moved
   number is the primary span: 10.808 -> 10.184 cu.

4. The bias field (3.911 cu) needs its decomposition to be read
   honestly. It is the radius-probe end sensitivity, and under the
   contiguity rule it no longer means erosion: the HIGH end (the
   artifact-corrected one) moves only 0.024 cu across probes at 0.5x,
   1x, and 2x contact radius; 3.89 of the 3.91 is the 0.5x probe
   fragmenting the ridge's sparse south half (at half radius a 0.53 cu
   stretch of the south half has no contact points, so the main-run
   heuristic switches to the dense northern run and t_lo jumps). The
   south half is real: it is continuous at 1x and 2x radius, and the
   tape physically ran its full length. The honest reading: the
   corrected end is stable; the probe flags the south half as
   low-density; the empirical bound on scale error is the independent
   fallback cross-check, not this field.

5. NOT blind, stated plainly. This run was made with the field numbers
   already known. Its defense is not blindness; it is that the fix is a
   principled cloud-side rule (threshold derived from the two void
   regimes, not from the tape), it was corroborated by two independent
   checks before adoption (fallback tape and GPS plausibility), and both
   runs are reported side by side, failure first.
units: cloud units (cu); one tape number converts, later

scale_candidate_primary.tape_plan: on roof, along the line; BOTH ends are eroded edge zone, bias is one-sided (reads short)

scale_candidate_fallback.tape_plan: on roof: hook the drip edge, run up the slope (divergence 0.32 deg, pos-sens 0.045 cu)
